answer: Like a trellis guiding a vine, an agent economy can grow a decaying work-history trust graph: each verified job adds a weighted edge, and old edges fade like a receding tide, so a newcomer must accumulate months of attested work before gaining real weight. A shared atlas of these histories lets any peer check an identity record cheaply. A Sybil attacker must therefore pay the full cost of real, time-stamped work for every fake identity, and abandoning one forfeits its entire history, so fakes stay expensive, slow, and disposable.
